- **The enum** has six real plates plus "Default" (`PrintConfig.hpp:314-322`). The stored names are at `PrintConfig.cpp:469-477`.
- **Display labels** come from `PrintConfig.cpp:1092-1097`: "Smooth Cool Plate", "Engineering Plate", "Smooth High Temp Plate", "Textured PEI Plate", "Textured Cool Plate" and "Cool Plate (SuperTack)".
  - There is no "Satin" and no "Smooth PEI". The closest to Smooth PEI is "High Temp Plate", shown as "Smooth High Temp Plate".
- **`curr_bed_type` belongs to the project**, not to the printer preset (project options list, `PresetBundle.cpp:53`). So it cannot be saved into a printer preset.
- **Saving:** each plate's own value goes into the 3MF as `bed_type` metadata (`bbs_3mf.cpp:7921-7924`). The global value lives in `project_config`. I believe it lands in `Metadata/project_settings.config` (`bbs_3mf.cpp:210`), but that is inference.
- **Per-plate override:** a plate falls back to the global value when it has none of its own (`PartPlate.cpp:188-204`). The per-plate choice in PlateSettingsDialog is disabled for every non-Bambu printer (`PlateSettingsDialog.cpp:408-409`).

## 2. `default_bed_type`
- **It is a printer-preset option.** It is defined at `PrintConfig.cpp:1100-1106` with the comment "won't be shown in the UI", and it is in the printer options list (`Preset.cpp:1384`). It is absent from `Tab.cpp`, so the Printer settings tab does not show it, but a user preset will save it.
- **In printer-model files it does nothing in Orca's C++.** The code that reads model files (`PresetBundle.cpp:~4700-4810`) has no key for it. About 40 model files carry it anyway (Creality K-series, all Bambu models, Flashforge AD5M and others).
- **Text values don't work; I'm treating this as an upstream bug.** `Preset::get_default_bed_type` (`Preset.cpp:966-994`) runs `atoi` on the value:
  - `"4"` gives Textured PEI, as intended.
  - `"Textured PEI Plate"` reads as 0, logs an error and falls back to High Temp Plate, even though the option's own description says text is supported.

1. **Bambu printers, or presets with `support_multi_bed_types` on:** the plate list is rebuilt. Orca then reads `app_config printer_settings[<preset name>]["curr_bed_type"]`. If that memory exists it wins; if not, `get_default_bed_type()` decides.

The value still matters, because it decides which filament bed-temperature setting the slice uses (`Tab.cpp:4320-4338`). 3. **Orca also remembers the last plate per preset name** in its app config, not in the preset file. It is written whenever the plate changes (`Plater.cpp:9478-9480`) and on export (`PresetBundle.cpp:2938`).

A brand-new preset name has none. Once the person picks a plate in the sidebar, the memory overrides the preset from then on.

No profile supports this. The Prusa MK4 and Ender-3 V2 model files have no `default_bed_type`, so the annotation would have to come from our own data.

## 6. Fork code (all under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`)
- **`PrinterCatalog.cpp:139, 164`** reads the model file's `default_bed_type` text, a field Orca itself ignores.
- **`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:86-93`** (it is in `PrinterSetup/`, not `Shell/`) shows the preset's `default_bed_type` text directly. This can disagree with what Orca actually picks. For example, the X1 Carbon file says "Textured PEI Plate" while Orca chooses Cool Plate (my inference from the code above).
- **`SetupCommands.cpp:511-526`** `select_bed_type` goes through `set_bed_type_accord_combox`, so Orca handles the project write and the per-preset memory itself.
- **`Printers/`** has no plate handling.

## Verdict
- **Can the plate be saved with the printer without a new setting?** Yes. Write a number into the user printer preset's existing `default_bed_type`; never text.
- **Will new projects start on it?** Yes, until the person picks another plate in the sidebar. After that, Orca's remembered value for that preset name wins. That memory sits in Orca's app config, so it isn't stored with the printer. I expect renaming the printer to lose it (inference).

  - It splits the model's `nozzle_diameter` on `;` (:138).
  - It drops a variant when no machine profile resolves for it (:149).
- **Counts** from my Python copy of the loader (`scratchpad/catalog.py`):
  - 987 model+nozzle variants across all vendor files, 983 after the OrcaArena exclusion.
  - 383 models (out of 384 index entries; the missing one is OrcaArena's).

- **How `split_brand` names brands** (:229, fork): it takes the brand from the start of the model's name when that matches the vendor name ignoring case and punctuation. That gives:
  - "Bambu Lab" for vendor file `BBL`, whose `name` is "Bambulab".
  - "BLOCKS" for vendor file `Blocks`.
  - A split brand: "Seckit Go3" becomes brand "Seckit" while "SecKit SK-Tank" stays "SecKit". A Brand select would show two entries unless it groups by `vendor_id`.
  - Models whose names don't start with the brand keep the vendor name as the brand, e.g. Volumic "EXO65".
- **Order** follows `directory_iterator`, which has no defined order (my inference), so the popup should sort brands itself.

- **How many sizes per model:** 181 models ship one size, 16 ship two, 37 three, 125 four, 11 five, 4 six and 9 eight. So 202 models ship more than one.

- **The sets vary a lot.** There are 27 distinct sets using 16 sizes: 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.75, 3, 5 and 8.

- **`run_wizard` opens Orca's web-based GuideFrame, not ConfigWizard.** At `GUI_App.cpp:8942` the ConfigWizard lines are commented out (`//auto wizard_t = new ConfigWizard(mainframe);`). `SP_PRINTERS` maps to `GuideFrame::BBL_MODELS_ONLY`, then it calls `wizard.run()` and, on success, `load_current_presets()`. Upstream: identical at 3ffb9585d2:8810. GuideFrame applies with `overwrite = true`, passing the page's full selection (`WebGuideDialog.cpp:956-962`); upstream (the one later change, 8ccae50e1b, appears to be an upstream PR).
- **`install_and_select_printer`** (`SetupCommands.cpp:439`, fork):
  1. Snapshots the vendors and filaments, for rollback.
  2. Calls `apply_vendor_config(vendors, filaments, config, false, model, variant, default_filament)`, where `false` means merge.
  3. Finds the system preset by model and variant and selects it inside `update_objects_position_when_select_preset`.
  4. Calls `export_selections`.

- **`apply_vendor_config` is upstream:** present at 3ffb9585d2 `PresetBundle.cpp:1138`, and the fork's diff hunks don't touch it. Its steps:
  - **Copy:** if `data_dir()/system/<vendor>.json` is missing, it copies the vendor JSON and its whole folder from resources (:1182, `install_vendor_bundles_from_resources` in `utils.cpp:1671`, upstream). Pictures, models and 3MFs are filtered out. That is about 4.1 MB of JSON for Creality and 4.8 MB for BBL. A vendor that is already installed is not copied again. Kenneth's `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin/system/` currently holds only `Custom.json` and `OrcaFilamentLibrary.json`, so vendors really are copied on demand.
  - **Reload:** `load_presets` (:1277) reloads every vendor bundle in `system/`, in parallel with TBB. Each bundle is loaded whole, all models' presets, with visibility set by `set_visible_from_appconfig` (`Preset.cpp:853`, upstream). It then reloads user presets and selections.
  - **Filaments are added, not replaced** when `overwrite = false` (:1258-1262). For an Ender-3 V2 that means its machine default filament is added.
- **Speed (my inference, not measured):** it is a startup-sized preset reload plus, the first time, a multi-megabyte copy. I'd expect sub-second to a few seconds depending on how many vendors are installed.

Yes, on this path. With `overwrite = false`, the old vendor map gets the new vendor, model and variant inserted into it (`PresetBundle.cpp:1264-1273`). Only the wizard path (`overwrite = true`) replaces the whole map.

## 5. Printer pictures
Every one of the 383 models has a `<model>_cover.png`; there are 386 cover files in total. The catalog already carries the path as `artwork_path` / `picture` (:140).

## 6. Naming
- **`add_named_printer`** (`NamedPrinters.cpp:184`, fork) requires the selected preset to be a system preset. It calls `Tab::save_preset(name)`, which saves a user printer preset that inherits the selected system preset. It records a device link when there is a device id, and if that device already has a printer it reuses it. The name comes from `first_free_printer_name`, which adds " (2)", " (3)" and so on (`PrinterNames.cpp:20`).
- **`name_installed_printers`** (:302, fork) finds the newly enabled models and, for each one, selects its system preset and calls `add_named_printer(plater, model.model, {})`.
- **Creality Ender-3 V2 0.4** would be named **"Creality Ender-3 V2"**: the model name, with no nozzle. On the panel path, `add_printer` uses `request.name`, or `model_id` when that's empty (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:178`), and `model_id` is that same model name. The system preset is "Creality Ender-3 V2 0.4 nozzle", so the name doesn't collide.

## Verdict
The brand, model and nozzle lists can come from `panel_printers()` unchanged. Two things to handle in the popup:
- **Nozzle control:** it has to show each model's own sizes. A fixed 0.25/0.4/0.6/0.8 set is wrong for most models; 181 models ship a single size (171 of them 0.4 only), and up to 8 sizes appear. A one-size model would want the control hidden or pre-chosen.
- **Brands:** sort them, and group by `vendor_id` to fold the SecKit/Seckit split.

The install step is already written: `OrcaPrinterBackend::add_printer` runs `install_and_select_printer` then `add_named_printer`, which merges rather than replaces and rolls back on failure. Its cost is one full upstream preset reload, plus a one-time copy of the vendor's files the first time a vendor is installed (inference; not timed).</result>

<result>I answered all six questions from the code and the shipped profiles; nothing was edited or run. The main finding: the mockup's three rows don't come from any data in the app, and for the MK4 two of them can't appear in any MK4-specific list. No Prusament profile is compatible with the MK4 at all.

**1. Is there real per-model data?**

There are two upstream fields.

- **`default_materials`** is on the model file (`Prusa MK4.json:11`, `Creality Ender-3 V2.json:11`, `Bambu Lab P1S.json:12`). It is parsed at `src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:369-378`. Orca's setup wizard uses it to tick filaments when you pick a model (`WebGuideDialog.cpp:446-486`). The old `ConfigWizard.cpp:2137-2160` path does the same, but `run_wizard` now opens the web wizard (`GUI_App.cpp:8975-8979`). `load_installed_filaments` also installs these when a printer has no compatible filament installed (`PresetBundle.cpp:2552-2588`). All of this is upstream.
- **`default_filament_profile`** is on the nozzle profile and is a single entry. Examples: `Prusa MK4 0.4 nozzle.json:10-12`, `Creality Ender-3 V2 0.4 nozzle.json:9-11`, and for the P1S it is inherited from `fdm_bbl_3dp_001_common.json:21-23`.
- **Compatibility** comes from `is_compatible_with_printer` (`Preset.cpp:809-841`, upstream). The sidebar list shows filaments that are both installed (`is_visible`) and compatible. The fork's chip uses the same two flags (`SetupCommands.cpp:200-220`).
- **Compatible counts at 0.4 mm** (my own script over the profile files):
  - MK4: 10 Prusa presets.
  - Ender-3 V2: 6 Creality presets.
  - P1S: 219 BBL presets.
  - Every printer also gets the 234 OrcaFilamentLibrary presets, which include eSUN PLA+ and PolyTerra PLA. Their `compatible_printers` is empty, so they fit any printer unless a vendor ships a preset with the same name (`Preset.cpp:3704-3725`, `819-823`).
- **Prusament** profiles exist only for the CORE One and XL; none lists the MK4.

**2. What the fork does with filaments**

- `PrinterCatalog.cpp:160-163` reads `default_filament_profile` after resolving the inheritance chain (`resolve_machine`, lines 50-63). It keeps one entry per nozzle size (lines 271-290).
- `install_and_select_printer` (`SetupCommands.cpp:439-516`) passes that one filament as both the "filaments to install" list and the preferred filament to `apply_vendor_config`.
  - With `overwrite=false` it adds the filament to the installed list without removing any (`PresetBundle.cpp:1248-1255`).
  - It then makes it the active slot-1 filament (lines 1281-1295) and saves the selections (line 1298).
  - So it installs and selects exactly one filament preset.
- `apply_vendor_config` is upstream (present at `3ffb9585d2:src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp:1138`).

**3. Searching by brand or material**

- Every preset carries `filament_vendor` and `filament_type`.
  - Generic presets inherit `"Generic"` (for example `Prusa/filament/fdm_filament_common.json:96`).
  - Branded ones name the brand: `"eSUN"`, `"Polymaker"`, `"Bambu Lab"`.
- The fork already reads both fields: `SetupCommands.cpp:51-68` and the `FilamentInfo` struct at `SetupCommands.hpp:40-52`.
- Uninstalled presets can be listed without reading the resource files, with one limit.
  - Orca loads every vendor bundle in the user's system folder, installed filaments or not, and only marks the installed ones visible (`Preset.cpp:865-868`).
  - The filament library bundle is always copied there (`PresetUpdater.cpp:1078`), but other vendors only once they are enabled (inferred from `PresetBundle.cpp:2195-2235`).
  - So library filaments are always listable. Prusa's own presets are listable only after the Prusa bundle is enabled; before that they exist only in `resources/profiles`.
- Installing a filament means setting `filaments/<name>=true` in app config (`AppConfig.cpp:47`). Orca does this from the wizard's filament page; `apply_vendor_config` is the programmatic route.
- There is no fork filament catalog. What exists is `compatible_filaments()` (installed and compatible only), `open_filament_library()` which opens Orca's own Add/Remove page (`SetupCommands.cpp:556-562`), and the chip menu that uses both (`FilamentMenu.cpp:426-454`).

**4. Per-printer memory of slots and colours**

This is upstream.
- `export_selections` writes, per printer name, the slot-1 filament, `filament_01…`, `filament_colors`, colour types and more into app config's `orca_presets` (`PresetBundle.cpp:2934-2960`, `AppConfig.cpp:801-803`, `1018-1019`).
- It is read back at startup (`load_selections`, lines 2723-2800) and on every printer switch when the "Remember printer configuration" preference is on, which is the default (`Tab.cpp:6229-6233`, `AppConfig.cpp:436-437`).
- A printer with no saved colours gets `#26A69A` in every slot (`PresetBundle.cpp:2657`).

Traced, partly inferred: after adding a printer with filament X, `apply_vendor_config` saves the selections with X in slot 1. Switching back to that printer later restores X. A new project keeps whatever is currently selected (inferred).

Not verified: whether the memory carries over to the person's named copy that `Printers::add_named_printer` saves (`NamedPrinters.cpp:201`).

**5. Syncing from the printer's trays**

- Upstream `Sidebar::sync_ams_list` (`Plater.cpp:3501`) needs a connected, selected machine. Otherwise it shows a "not connected" warning (lines 3505-3515).
- The fork already wires this up:
  - `sync_from_printer` (`SetupCommands.cpp:565-588`) requires a named printer with a connected device.
  - `printer_trays()` (lines 287-307) reports whether trays are available.
  - The chip has a "Use what's loaded on the printer…" row (`FilamentMenu.cpp:327-342`).
  - The add-printer code reads trays live: Bambu trays at `PrinterDiscovery.cpp:24-60`, Moonraker multi-filament lanes at `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:113-116`. These are fork structs called `spools`, but they are only device reports, nothing saved.
- Inference: sync during add-printer is possible only after the connection step has succeeded, or for a printer the app has already discovered and that reports its trays. It is never possible for a printer added by model alone.

**6. Colour**

- Picking a preset applies its `default_filament_colour` if it has one, and otherwise leaves the slot's colour unchanged. That is upstream `PresetComboBox.cpp:252-253`, mirrored by the fork at `SetupCommands.cpp:330-332`.
- Nearly all shipped presets leave it empty: 788 of about 840 values are `""`. That includes Prusa Generic PLA @MK4, eSUN PLA+ and PolyTerra PLA.
- Colours are always hex values: the project's `filament_colour` and trays' `#RRGGBB`. The colour grid tooltip shows the hex key (`FilamentMenu.cpp:167`).
- A colour word would only be needed if the mockup labelled rows by colour. Nothing in the data supplies one.

**(a) Does "Common on the <model>" have a data source?**

There is no data on what is common. The closest real field is `default_materials`, the wizard's ticks:
- **MK4:** "Prusa Generic PLA-CF; Prusa Generic PC; Prusa Generic PVA; Prusa Generic PA; Prusa Generic PA-CF; Prusa Generic ABS @MK4; Prusa Generic PLA @MK4; Prusa Generic PETG @MK4; Prusa Generic TPU @MK4; Prusa Generic ASA @MK4". There is no Prusament, eSUN or Polymaker.
- **Ender-3 V2:** "Creality Generic PLA; Creality Generic PETG; Creality Generic ABS".
- **P1S:** "Bambu PLA Matte, Bambu PLA Basic, Bambu PLA-CF, Bambu PETG-CF, Bambu ABS, Bambu PLA Silk, Bambu PAHT-CF, Bambu Support For PLA, Bambu Support For PA/PET, Generic PLA, Generic PLA High Speed, Generic PETG, Bambu PETG HF". All the Bambu-branded entries end in "@BBL X1C".

Otherwise it uses the Orca agent or the preset's own `printer_agent` (`GUI_App.cpp:3572-3586`, upstream; the fake-mode line at 3576-3578 is fork).
  - Swapping agents removes the old agent's SSDP callback (`NetworkAgent.cpp:116-134`, upstream).
  - The Orca agent's discovery is an empty stub (`OrcaPrinterAgent.cpp:61-64`, upstream).
  - **So with a non-Bambu preset selected, no SSDP results reach the device list.**
- **Where discovery is started:**

1. Which printers can appear: Bambu Lab only. LAN printers found by SSDP need the plug-in and the Bambu agent active, which today means a Bambu preset is selected. Cloud-bound printers need a Bambu sign-in. No other brand is found in the background.

The main finding: the mockup's three rows don't come from any data in the app, and for the MK4 two of them can't appear in any MK4-specific list. No Prusament profile is compatible with the MK4 at all.

**1. Is there real per-model data?**

There are two upstream fields.

- **`default_materials`** is on the model file (`Prusa MK4.json:11`, `Creality Ender-3 V2.json:11`, `Bambu Lab P1S.json:12`). It is parsed at `src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:369-378`. Orca's setup wizard uses it to tick filaments when you pick a model (`WebGuideDialog.cpp:446-486`). The old `ConfigWizard.cpp:2137-2160` path does the same, but `run_wizard` now opens the web wizard (`GUI_App.cpp:8975-8979`). `load_installed_filaments` also installs these when a printer has no compatible filament installed (`PresetBundle.cpp:2552-2588`). All of this is upstream.
- **`default_filament_profile`** is on the nozzle profile and is a single entry. Examples: `Prusa MK4 0.4 nozzle.json:10-12`, `Creality Ender-3 V2 0.4 nozzle.json:9-11`, and for the P1S it is inherited from `fdm_bbl_3dp_001_common.json:21-23`.
- **Compatibility** comes from `is_compatible_with_printer` (`Preset.cpp:809-841`, upstream). The sidebar list shows filaments that are both installed (`is_visible`) and compatible. The fork's chip uses the same two flags (`SetupCommands.cpp:200-220`).
- **Compatible counts at 0.4 mm** (my own script over the profile files):
  - MK4: 10 Prusa presets.
  - Ender-3 V2: 6 Creality presets.
  - P1S: 219 BBL presets.
  - Every printer also gets the 234 OrcaFilamentLibrary presets, which include eSUN PLA+ and PolyTerra PLA. Their `compatible_printers` is empty, so they fit any printer unless a vendor ships a preset with the same name (`Preset.cpp:3704-3725`, `819-823`).
- **Prusament** profiles exist only for the CORE One and XL; none lists the MK4.

**2. What the fork does with filaments**

- `PrinterCatalog.cpp:160-163` reads `default_filament_profile` after resolving the inheritance chain (`resolve_machine`, lines 50-63). It keeps one entry per nozzle size (lines 271-290).
- `install_and_select_printer` (`SetupCommands.cpp:439-516`) passes that one filament as both the "filaments to install" list and the preferred filament to `apply_vendor_config`.
  - With `overwrite=false` it adds the filament to the installed list without removing any (`PresetBundle.cpp:1248-1255`).
  - It then makes it the active slot-1 filament (lines 1281-1295) and saves the selections (line 1298).
  - So it installs and selects exactly one filament preset.
- `apply_vendor_config` is upstream (present at `3ffb9585d2:src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp:1138`).

**3. Searching by brand or material**

- Every preset carries `filament_vendor` and `filament_type`.
  - Generic presets inherit `"Generic"` (for example `Prusa/filament/fdm_filament_common.json:96`).
  - Branded ones name the brand: `"eSUN"`, `"Polymaker"`, `"Bambu Lab"`.
- The fork already reads both fields: `SetupCommands.cpp:51-68` and the `FilamentInfo` struct at `SetupCommands.hpp:40-52`.
- Uninstalled presets can be listed without reading the resource files, with one limit.
  - Orca loads every vendor bundle in the user's system folder, installed filaments or not, and only marks the installed ones visible (`Preset.cpp:865-868`).
  - The filament library bundle is always copied there (`PresetUpdater.cpp:1078`), but other vendors only once they are enabled (inferred from `PresetBundle.cpp:2195-2235`).
  - So library filaments are always listable. Prusa's own presets are listable only after the Prusa bundle is enabled; before that they exist only in `resources/profiles`.
- Installing a filament means setting `filaments/<name>=true` in app config (`AppConfig.cpp:47`). Orca does this from the wizard's filament page; `apply_vendor_config` is the programmatic route.
- There is no fork filament catalog. What exists is `compatible_filaments()` (installed and compatible only), `open_filament_library()` which opens Orca's own Add/Remove page (`SetupCommands.cpp:556-562`), and the chip menu that uses both (`FilamentMenu.cpp:426-454`).

**4. Per-printer memory of slots and colours**

This is upstream.
- `export_selections` writes, per printer name, the slot-1 filament, `filament_01…`, `filament_colors`, colour types and more into app config's `orca_presets` (`PresetBundle.cpp:2934-2960`, `AppConfig.cpp:801-803`, `1018-1019`).
- It is read back at startup (`load_selections`, lines 2723-2800) and on every printer switch when the "Remember printer configuration" preference is on, which is the default (`Tab.cpp:6229-6233`, `AppConfig.cpp:436-437`).
- A printer with no saved colours gets `#26A69A` in every slot (`PresetBundle.cpp:2657`).

Traced, partly inferred: after adding a printer with filament X, `apply_vendor_config` saves the selections with X in slot 1. Switching back to that printer later restores X. A new project keeps whatever is currently selected (inferred).

Not verified: whether the memory carries over to the person's named copy that `Printers::add_named_printer` saves (`NamedPrinters.cpp:201`).

**5. Syncing from the printer's trays**

- Upstream `Sidebar::sync_ams_list` (`Plater.cpp:3501`) needs a connected, selected machine. Otherwise it shows a "not connected" warning (lines 3505-3515).
- The fork already wires this up:
  - `sync_from_printer` (`SetupCommands.cpp:565-588`) requires a named printer with a connected device.
  - `printer_trays()` (lines 287-307) reports whether trays are available.
  - The chip has a "Use what's loaded on the printer…" row (`FilamentMenu.cpp:327-342`).

- Inference: sync during add-printer is possible only after the connection step has succeeded, or for a printer the app has already discovered and that reports its trays. It is never possible for a printer added by model alone.

**6. Colour**

- Picking a preset applies its `default_filament_colour` if it has one, and otherwise leaves the slot's colour unchanged. That is upstream `PresetComboBox.cpp:252-253`, mirrored by the fork at `SetupCommands.cpp:330-332`.
- Nearly all shipped presets leave it empty: 788 of about 840 values are `""`. That includes Prusa Generic PLA @MK4, eSUN PLA+ and PolyTerra PLA.
- Colours are always hex values: the project's `filament_colour` and trays' `#RRGGBB`. The colour grid tooltip shows the hex key (`FilamentMenu.cpp:167`).
- A colour word would only be needed if the mockup labelled rows by colour. Nothing in the data supplies one.

- "Pick it later" can simply keep the profile default, which is what happens today.

- **Search field:** "Search brand or material".
- **List heading:** "Suggested for the MK4". This is honest because it is the profile's own list; "Common on" claims usage data the app doesn't have.
- **Link:** "Skip — use OrcaSlicer's default (Prusa Generic PLA)".</result>

content.text:
Here's the feasibility report: the agents' findings, checked by me against the code. I've spot-checked the key claims.

The popup can be built in the printer chat's React page, using printer-setup code that already exists. Brand, model, nozzle and saving the printer can come from current code with almost no new plumbing. Three parts of the design show things OrcaSlicer doesn't hold: printers of any brand found on the network, the "Satin" and "Smooth PEI" plates, and a "Common on the MK4" list of filament brands. Each section below says what we can actually show instead. Five decisions at the end need your answer before I build.

## 1. "Found on your network"

- **Only Bambu Lab printers can be found today.**
  - The fork's `discover_printers()` (`PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp:76-85`) reads OrcaSlicer's `DeviceManager::get_my_machine_list()` (`DeviceCore/DevManager.cpp:651-675`, upstream).
  - That list holds Bambu printers bound to a signed-in Bambu account, plus LAN printers the app already has an access code for. A brand-new printer with no access code sits only in `get_local_machinelist()`. The fork's `connection()` reads that fuller list at `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:335-347`.
- **Bambu's LAN search has two preconditions**, both upstream:
  - It needs Bambu's network plug-in installed (`BBLPrinterAgent.cpp:104-113`).
  - It needs the Bambu printer agent active, which OrcaSlicer only picks when a Bambu printer profile is selected (`GUI_App.cpp:3572-3586`).
- **Other brands are only searched on demand.** OrcaSlicer's OctoPrint mDNS browse (`BonjourDialog.cpp:126`), the Creality K-series scan and the Flashforge broadcast all run only from the Browse button in the physical-printer dialog (`PhysicalPrinterDialog.cpp:212-256`, upstream). Moonraker has no discovery at all.
- **What picking a found printer can set at once:**
  - The model: the device reports a model id, for example C12 for the P1S, and the fork's catalogue maps it (`PrinterCatalog.cpp:137,182`).
  - The link between the saved printer and that device. `add_printer` already accepts a device id and records the link (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:177`, `Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp:184-206`, fork), but nothing passes one today (`PrinterConversation.cpp:503-506`).
- **What waits for "connect":**
  - The nozzle. It is unknown until the printer reports it after connecting (`DevNozzleSystem.h:18`, upstream). We'd assume 0.4, and the fork's existing nozzle-mismatch check flags it after connecting (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:383-387`).
  - The access code, selecting the machine, and verifying the connection.
- **The printer chat's Add opening already shows this same found-printer list** (`PrinterConversation.cpp:175-185`).
- **The fake Bambu printer connects itself instantly** (`Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp:521-547`). It can test a found row, but never the "found, not yet connected" state.

## 2. Plate

- **The plate belongs to the project, not the printer.** `curr_bed_type` is a project setting (`PresetBundle.cpp:53`, upstream).
- **OrcaSlicer remembers the last plate per printer name anyway.** When a printer is selected, it uses that memory first, and the printer profile's hidden `default_bed_type` otherwise (`Plater.cpp:2518-2531`, upstream).
  - Calling the fork's existing `select_bed_type` (`SetupCommands.cpp:511`) right after saving writes that memory, exactly as a plate pick in the sidebar does. No new setting is needed.
  - Inference: the memory is keyed by name, so it is probably lost if the printer is renamed.
- **Most non-Bambu printers have no plate choice.** OrcaSlicer shows the plate dropdown only for Bambu printers or profiles with `support_multi_bed_types` on (`Plater.cpp:2512, 2545`). The MK4 and Ender 3 V2 profiles have it off.
- **OrcaSlicer has six plates:** Smooth Cool, Engineering, Smooth High Temp, Textured PEI, Textured Cool and SuperTack (`PrintConfig.cpp:1092-1097`). There is no "Satin" and no "Smooth PEI".
- **"Ships with the MK4" has no source.** About 40 model files name a default plate, but the MK4's doesn't.

## 3. Filament ("spool")

- **"Common on the MK4" has no data behind it.**
  - The nearest real field is the model's `default_materials`, the list OrcaSlicer's setup wizard pre-ticks (upstream).
  - For the MK4 that is ten "Prusa Generic …" presets (`Prusa MK4.json:11`). There is no Prusament, eSUN or Polymaker.
  - Every Prusament profile lists only the CORE One as compatible (`Prusament PLA @CORE One.json:15`), so Prusament PLA can never appear for an MK4.
  - eSUN PLA+ and PolyTerra PLA exist only in OrcaSlicer's general filament library, which fits every printer.
- **What step 3 can honestly do:** pick one filament preset to start with.
  - The fork's `install_and_select_printer` already installs one filament preset and puts it in slot 1, through upstream `apply_vendor_config` (`SetupCommands.cpp:439-509`).
  - OrcaSlicer's per-printer memory of slots and colours then brings it back whenever this printer is selected (`PresetBundle.cpp:2934-2960`). Whether that memory carries over to the person's named copy is unverified.
- **Tray sync is impossible here.** It needs a connected printer (`Plater.cpp:3501-3515`), and a printer being added isn't connected yet.
- **No colour words are needed.** Most presets set no colour.

## 4. Brand, model, nozzle

- **The catalogue covers vendors the person hasn't installed.** The fork's catalogue reads every packaged vendor (`PrinterCatalog.cpp:98-106`): 64 brands, 383 models, 983 model-and-nozzle combinations.
- **Nozzle sizes vary per model, so the control has to show each model's own sizes.**
  - 181 models ship one size, and some ship up to eight.
  - The MK4 ships 0.25 / 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8; the Ender 3 V2 ships 0.4 only.
  - With one size, I'd hide the control.
- **Two brand spellings need folding.** The catalogue splits SecKit and Seckit into two brands, so I'd group by vendor file.
- **Installing is already written and safe.** `add_printer` adds the new model to the person's setup without removing anything, and rolls back on failure (upstream `PresetBundle.cpp:1264-1273`).
  - The first printer from a vendor copies that vendor's profiles into the data folder, about 4 MB for Creality, then reloads all presets. I haven't timed it.
- **Today's button opens OrcaSlicer's web setup guide**, not the old ConfigWizard (`GUI_App.cpp`, `run_wizard`, upstream).

## 5. Gaps in the design itself

- **No buttons.** None of the three boards draws Back, Next, Cancel or a close button, so nothing on step 1 moves forward.
- **Mismatched examples.** Step 1 shows an Ender 3 V2, steps 2 and 3 talk about the MK4, and the Ender 3 V2 only ships a 0.4 nozzle.
- **Different screen.** The boards draw the popup over the Prepare screen. In code, the manual path starts from the printer chat on Home. The popup would open over that chat.

## Decisions for you

**1. Should the network list show only Bambu printers the app has already found, without starting a search itself?**
- (a) Show what OrcaSlicer's device list already holds, including new printers that have no access code yet, and hide the section when it's empty. This has no side effects, but on a computer with a non-Bambu printer selected and no Bambu sign-in it will usually be empty.
- (b) Start Bambu's search when the popup opens. This finds more, but it swaps the network provider of the currently selected non-Bambu printer until its profile next changes, and it does nothing without Bambu's plug-in.
- (c) Drop the section. The printer chat's opening already lists found printers.

I recommend (a). Picking a row fills in brand and model and pre-selects 0.4. The saved printer is linked to that device, and connecting stays a separate step.

**2. Should step 2 only appear for printers where OrcaSlicer offers a plate choice?**
- (a) Show it only for Bambu printers and profiles with multiple plate types, using OrcaSlicer's own plate names. Other printers get a two-step popup. The choice is saved as OrcaSlicer's per-printer plate memory, the same as a sidebar pick.
- (b) Always ask, and turn on `support_multi_bed_types` in the saved printer so the sidebar shows the plate. This changes a printer setting the vendor left off.
- (c) Always ask, and store the answer where nothing shows it. People would make a choice they never see again.

I recommend (a).

**3. Should step 3 become "Which filament do you want to start with?"** Under it would sit a list headed "Suggested for the MK4", taken from the model's `default_materials`. A search would cover filaments compatible with that printer. The skip link would read "Skip — start with Prusa Generic PLA @MK4", the profile's own default.
- Yes, as worded.
- Yes, with your wording.
- Something else.

I recommend yes, as worded. It drops "spool" and the invented "Common on" list, and claims only what the profiles say.

**4. Should I add the missing Back, Next and Cancel controls in code first, or should the canvas boards be updated first?**
- (a) Code first. The controls would follow the printer chat's existing dialog buttons: Next on step 1, choosing a row in steps 2 and 3 moves on, Back returns, Cancel or Escape closes with nothing saved. I'd send you light and dark captures of each step and update the canvas after you approve.
- (b) Canvas first. This waits on a design pass before any code.

I recommend (a).

**5. When the printer chat page fails to load, should its native fallback button keep opening OrcaSlicer's printer list?**
- (a) Keep OrcaSlicer's printer list there (`PrinterPanel.cpp:108-113`). The React popup can't appear when the page itself failed, and this case is rare.
- (b) Build a second, native version of the popup just for this case. That is a lot of code for a rare failure.

I recommend (a).

Nothing is built yet. The work would happen in a new worktree, `.claude/worktrees/add-printer-popup` on branch `claude/add-printer-popup`, which I cut from jusprin-newui at `1cbce387d8`. None of this needs a live AI model call.

content.content:
# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.
# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.

### 5. One seam beats many touch points

**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.

### 10. Pull direction dominates every local edit

**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.

**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.

**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them
into the strip at construction. The Phase 1 production shell reached a
19-added-line upstream footprint this way where the POC's reparenting shell
needed edits across eight upstream files.

The same measurement gives the rule for every fork-owned screen that comes
after the shell. OrcaSlicer's surfaces (the stock homepage, Prepare, Preview,
Monitor, the settings tabs) stay inside the Notebook, because their
correctness depends on it. Fork-owned surfaces (the header, the Agent pane,
Home, and whatever follows) live outside it, as siblings of the Notebook in a
fork-owned sizer, shown and hidden by the shell. The shell *reads* the
Notebook's selection to decide what to show and *never edits its page list*:
no `RemovePage`, `InsertPage`, or reparenting of a stock page. Removing or
replacing a page hands the fork the meaning of that index. Upstream keeps
addressing it by number — `tpHome` as a dialog parent, the target of
`EVT_LOAD_URL`, the tab `post_init` returns to — and every one of those lands
on the fork's widget with no conflict and no error. If a fork surface truly
must be a page, append it last, where no upstream code addresses it.

Navigation between screens stays a Notebook selection change even when the
screen being left is fork-owned. Menu and shortcut enabling, undo and redo
availability, and slice-status updates all read `GetSelection()`, so the
selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.
Showing Prepare any other way leaves those predicates answering for the wrong
page, silently.

Some stock behavior is already exposed as an event idiom rather than a
function. Upstream itself drives plate slicing from two places with the same
sequence — the slice button and the Cmd+R shortcut both run
`plater->update(true, true)`, post `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_SLICE_PLATE` to the Plater,
and select the Preview tab — so fork code may repeat that short dispatch
without violating the shared-implementation rule; the behavior itself stays
owned by Plater's event handler.

Historical measurements and the incidents behind several of these rules are in the [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) and, for the spike era, in the [POC reference](poc-reference.md).
# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
